findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the wastewater pipe running into the grease trap to have a leak. There was a catch basin under the pipe to survey leaking water. There was also a notable odor in the back room which may be caused by the leaking grease trap. Ensure the plumbing is repaired to prevent cross-contamination. A follow-up will be conducted on November 9, 2026 to ensure the plumbing is repaired.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment:
2nd Repeat Violation
Observed no staff member on site to have a certified food protection manager certification. Ensure there is a CFPM on site at all times of operation.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed an employee fail to hand wash prior to donning gloves. Education was conducted regarding when to wash. Ensure handwashing is conducted prior to donning gloves to prevent cross-contamination.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed the hand washing sink in front area and back area of facility to be obstructed. Ensure hand sinks are cleared and accessible for use at all times. A follow-up will be conducted on 11/12/2026 to ensure compliance.
findings.citation_text: 5-203.11(A) Handwashing Sinks. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, at least 1 HANDWASHING SINK, a number of HANDWASHING SINKS necessary for their convenient use by EMPLOYEES in areas specified under § 5-204.11, and not fewer than the number of HANDWASHING SINKS required by LAW shall be provided.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment:
2nd Repeat Violation

Observed sink in back prep area to not have soap or paper towel available for use. Soap and paper towel were supplied during the inspection. Ensure sinks are fully supplied at all times to promote frequent handwashing.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Inspector observed no test strips for quaternary ammonia sanitizer present at the facility. The test strips are required for testing sanitizer for proper chemical concentration. The inspector will follow up on November 12, 2026 to ensure test strips are present and available in the facility.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation
Observed no staff member on site to have a certified food protection manager certification. Ensure there is a CFPM on site at all times of operation.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.comment:
Repeat violation 

Observed no signed employee health and reporting agreements for food employees at facility. Provide a signed employee health and reporting agreement for all food employees at facility. Agreements were provided during the inspection.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed hand washing sinks in front area and back area of facility to be inoperable due to either leaks or obstruction. Have hand sinks cleared and serviced by a licensed plumbing contractor. A follow-up will be conducted on 4/11/2025 to ensure compliance.
findings.citation_text: 5-203.11(A) Handwashing Sinks. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, at least 1 HANDWASHING SINK, a number of HANDWASHING SINKS necessary for their convenient use by EMPLOYEES in areas specified under § 5-204.11, and not fewer than the number of HANDWASHING SINKS required by LAW shall be provided.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed sink in front prep area to not have soap available for use. Soap dispenser was refilled during the inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Observed sink in employee bathroom to not have paper towels available for use. Paper towels were refilled during the inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Observed the back hand sink to be fully obstructed. Observed the front hand sink to have a mason jar of food and a lighter stored in the sink basin. The front hand sink was also obstructed by a rolling cart of food items. The hand sinks need to be accessible at all times for employee use. A follow-up will be conducted on 4/11/2025 to ensure compliance.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Observed food items stored on the floor in dry storage as well as below display tables in the display area. Food items need to be protected from pests and cross-contamination by being stored at least 6 inches off the floor at all times. Ensure proper food storage requirements are met in the facility. Proper food storage will be spot checked along with the follow-up conducted on 4/11/2025.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
findings.comment: Observed old mop water and drainage water from freeze-drying equipment to be retained in buckets in the facility. All wastewater needs to be efficiently conveyed and disposed through an approved sewage system. Wastewater cannot be retained onsite as it poses a risk of cross-contamination and pest development. The buckets were discarded during the inspection.
findings.citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed employees on duty at facility to not have food handler’s certification. All food employees at facility must have certified food manager or food handler training within 30 days of hire. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
Observed no certified food manager on duty during food preparation. A certified food manager must be present at facility during all times of food preparation and service. 

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.comment:

2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.

6-301.11: Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed hand washing sinks in front area and back area of facility to be inoperable due to leaks. Have hand sinks serviced by a licensed plumbing contractor. 

5-203.11: (A) Specified under LAW, facility must have a number of HANDWASHING SINKS necessary for their convenient use by EMPLOYEESS. (B) If APPROVED, automatic handwashing may be substituted. (C) IF APPROVED, chemically treated towelettes can be used.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
Observed employees on duty at facility to not have food handler certification. All food employees at facility must have certified food manager training or food handler training. 

410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.
